mail-29.subject: The Sunday Loaf #40: the flat loaf post-mortem
mail-29.body: Last week half of you wrote in about flat loaves. The short answer is under-proofed shaping or an exhausted starter, and the long answer is this issue. Also: a reader's question about baking at altitude, and why we stopped recommending the dutch-oven preheat at 260 °C.

mail-7.subject: The Sunday Loaf #41: sourdough for people who forget things
mail-7.body:
This week's letter.

The forgiving loaf. If you left your starter in the fridge for three weeks (hi), here is the schedule that still works: feed it Friday night, mix Saturday morning at 75% hydration, bulk in the oven with the light on, shape at 6 pm, cold-retard overnight, bake Sunday at 240 °C in a lidded pot for 20 minutes, then 25 uncovered.

Also in this issue: why a sharper blade matters less than a wetter one, and a reader's rye that we could not stop eating.

The Sunday Loaf goes to 4,100 people every week. Forward it to one of them.

Unsubscribe · Update preferences
